comment.comment: // runs to the end of the line. There are no /* */ comments.
comment.name: comment.line.double-slash.mtc

string.comment: Text is in double quotes only, and may run over several lines.
string.name: string.quoted.double.mtc

patterns.comment: The escapes Cogniscript reads: \a \b \e \f \n \r \t \v, \x41, \u00e9, octal \0 to \777, \cA, and a backslash before a mark that isn't a letter, digit or _, which is the mark itself.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.mtc

patterns.comment: Any other escape, such as \d or \_, fails the deploy: write \\d.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unknown-escape.mtc

patterns.comment: Code-pipeline hooks only: mt and the SDKs replace @promptJson(pipeline/name) and @schemaJson(pipeline/name) wherever they appear in a hook's file, before it is compiled. In an app they are plain text. A grammar can't tell a hook from an app, so they are marked in every .mtc, but only inside text, the one place they are useful.
patterns.name: keyword.control.directive.mtc

file-include.comment: @prompt("name") and @json("name"): the text of prompts/name.md or json/name.json, put into the program when it is compiled, in an app or a hook. In any case, with spaces allowed. Inside text it is plain text, which the string rule takes first.

number.comment: Digits with at most one decimal point, which may come first or last: 42, 19.99, .5, 5. No exponent, hex or separators.
number.name: constant.numeric.mtc

invalid-name.comment: A name is letters and digits, and may start with _ or a digit. An underscore after the first character fails the deploy, so retry_count is marked.
invalid-name.name: invalid.illegal.name.mtc

operator.comment: A single | or & is not an operator.
operator.name: keyword.operator.mtc
